narrative: OMX30 opens into a risk-off Friday with negative global signals dominating. The -0.648% correlation bias reflects contagion from NASDAQ's -2.60% collapse (AI concerns) and broad European weakness (DAX -0.77%, CAC -0.63%). Technicals are deeply oversold (Stoch K=2.4, RSI 37), offering mean-reversion bounce potential, but momentum remains broken: price is 3.3% below the 50-MA, MACD is below signal, and ADX shows moderate bearish DI bias. Oil's elevated level (~$110) will weigh on industrials and consumer discretion. The index sits 5.3% from 52W highs—classic late-cycle fatigue. With VIX +2.73% to 19.55 and US yields falling (-3.75% to 4.953%), the macro backdrop favors defensive rotation into pharma/healthcare, but broad-market gravity remains downward.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to open -0.3% to -0.7% on negative global signals and tech contagion. NASDAQ's -2.60% overnight and oil spike are headwinds; however, oversold Stochastics (K=2.4) suggest bounce risk intraday if sentiment stabilizes. Key support at 3085 (lower Bollinger band); resistance at 3180 (50-MA). Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—a miss could accelerate selloff. Sector call: Defensives (AstraZeneca, Essity) outperform on risk-off; Banks mixed (NIM support from higher yields offset by credit cycle uncertainty); Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco) pressured by oil costs and NASDAQ sentiment. USD/SEK at 9.936 (+0.48%) provides modest tailwind for Ericsson/Hexagon, but tech sentiment globally remains fragile. Avoid chasing; wait for Stochastic cross above 50 or close above 50-MA before re-engaging longs.
